chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: His reputation and first hearing Louis Armstrong on record
summary: He says he always played his own way, and first heard Armstrong's Cornet Chop Suey and Alligator Crawl on a victrola in Detroit.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, anyway, now at this point, were you starting to get a reputation being known - do you think - for yourself or as part of - not just the band - but you, yourself, were getting known as a hot trumpeter--- in Chicago---

Well, sort of -- you know -- I had to prove the point. You never know really how good you are -- who knows what people think of how you're playing. I never played like anybody else; I played my thing. And, what I thought was jazz.
And, at this point, just for the sake of all the people who are interested in this sort of thing -- at this point, you had not yet heard Louie Armstrong - is that correct?
You heard that one record--- by now---
You heard him in Detroit - okay.

On a record - that was the first time, in my hotel room with a wind-up victrola - I heard "Cornet Chop-Suey" and "Alligator Crawl" and I said, my God - who is that - that's it. Because I like the drive and I do that today--- I'm a drive -- I like to drive the melody, you know.
All right - so, but you hadn't heard
him in person at this point yet---
